title: Choose Halo's visual world
question: The roll assigned Dichroic Gallery. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Dichroic Gallery
options.lineage: dichroic glass installations: suspended coated panes in a white gallery, throwing shifting colored light onto walls and floor
options.thesis: Every component is a pane of coated glass hung in a bright room. Move it and the colored light it throws moves with it, so motion shows up as light. The category default it refuses is the dark neon dev-tool page.
materials: frosted pane with a dichroic edge
cast spectral light on a matte wall
options.viewport: A bright cool-white wall. Three live panes hang in space: a toast stack, a half-open drawer, and a spring curve. Each casts a cyan, magenta, or amber light pool that follows it on a spring. The headline 'Surfaces that move like they weigh something.' is set large at the left, with a working `npm i halo-ui-react` copy chip and 'Fire a toast' as the primary action. Pressing it drops a real toast into the stack.
options.risk: Glass on white can wash out. Contrast has to come from type weight and the cast light, not from borders.

raised.raise: Each section holds one frozen moment, a spring caught at its overshoot peak, and interacting releases it.
Layout snaps to a strict 8px detent grid, the same detents the drawer snaps to.
The spring mechanism is taught in numbered steps, with annotated diagrams of velocity handoff and projected snapping.
Cast light crosses section seams. Color thrown in one section lands on the next.

options.label: Frosted Partition
options.lineage: acid-etched office glass partitions, where people and objects behind them read as soft silhouettes
options.thesis: The page sits behind etched glass. Content sharpens as it comes forward and softens as it recedes.
options.viewport: A full-bleed etched pane with a blurred toast stack behind it. The headline is sharp in front, and hovering clears a disc through the frost.
options.risk: This is the literal glassmorphism reading most runs land on. It is familiar and tasteful, and easy to mistake for a template.

options.label: Silk Canopy Chords
options.lineage: translucent tensioned banners over a sunlit courtyard
options.thesis: Stacked toasts are translucent silk lanes, and where they overlap their colors mix into a chord that shows stack depth.
options.viewport: Horizontal silk lanes cross a bright field. Each lane is a live toast, and the overlaps mix color.
options.case: Overlap maps cleanly to stacking, but it is less legible as frosted glass, which the user pinned.
options.risk: It can read as an art piece rather than a component library.

options.label: VU Meter Bridge
options.thesis: Needles with real mass and damping are springs, so the site reads motion as instrument ballistics.
options.viewport: A row of meters, where each needle is a spring config, above a live toast.
options.case: Strong product clarity for springs, but it is an instrument costume and fights minimal frosted glass.
options.risk: It reads as a retro audio skin.

options.label: Wuxia Painted Hoarding
options.case: Developers don't identify with it, and it says nothing about glass.
options.kept: The single held moment: each section freezes a spring at its peak.

options.label: Azulejo Station Hall
options.kept: Whole-unit grid snapping that mirrors drawer detents.

options.label: Hand-drawn Zine
options.case: Too casual for 'clean, minimal, 2026', and cream paper is a known AI default.
options.kept: Stepwise teaching of a hard mechanism.

options.label: Itasha Vinyl Wrap
options.case: Too loud for minimal, and off-subject.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A component-library landing page: a centered headline, an install command, a live demo, then docs.
canonCard.viewport: A centered title, an npm command, and a 'Render a toast' button over a light grid.
